summary: Round 2 re-review of Task 07 at fc0b9e5 (round 1 reviewed 3dda490). Both round-1 findings are discharged and no regression in test quality was introduced: the change to tests/ is comment-only, and the change to src/ does not weaken any existing assertion. Finding 1 (the case 'произвольный порядок — одинокий half в конце' earns no regression protection) — the label is honest and clear enough; keep the case. It names the reason (input is the tail of the [full, half, full, half] case, expectation duplicates the one-group case), names the method (mutation testing), and closes with an unambiguous instruction to the next reader — 'защиту от регрессий за ним не считать'. I re-measured the claim at fc0b9e5 in an isolated worktree and widened it from three mutants to five: A identity-keying (re-sort input into GROUP_IDS order) → only 'перестановка разрывает пару' fails; B pair only at an even index → only 'соседние half образуют пару' fails; F half pairs with the next half found anywhere ahead → '[full, half, full, half]' and 'перестановка разрывает пару' fail; G alone only at the very last index → the same two fail; C trailing lone half classified as --full → 5 of 8 fail, the doc case among them but alongside four others (lines 32, 40, 54 and 'перестановка разрывает пару'). Across all five the doc case is never the sole killer, so the comment's universal phrasing is not misleading in practice, and deletion is no longer the better option — the case is now correctly priced. Finding 2 (the existence branch has no test and no owner) — the routing into Task 10 is right, and I verified it is actually executable rather than merely plausible: tests/harness/main.ts resetData() sends a snapshot carrying a 'version' field straight through migrateData, and I confirmed by probe at fc0b9e5 that migrateData survives a board whose groups object is missing a key (groupOrder still contains 'orgIntentions', groups does not) — the sanitization loop at migration.ts:156 iterates the groups that exist, so nothing throws before render. So the seeded scenario reaches BoardLayout as intended. Two cautions on the routing are in finding 1 below. The guard's new shape does not change the untested branch's reachability: I probed every value class that could tell Object.hasOwn apart from the old truthiness check, and all of them are already fatal earlier — a null-valued group key throws in migrateData ('Cannot read properties of null (reading title)'), a primitive-valued one throws too ('Cannot create property title on number 0'), and an empty-object value is treated identically by both forms (hasOwn true, truthy true). The swap is therefore pure hardening with no reachable behavioural delta, and the branch under test is the same branch as in round 1. Gates: npm test 87 passed, measured by me at fc0b9e5 in an isolated worktree. I deliberately did NOT run npx playwright test: playwright.config.ts pins port 5173 with reuseExistingServer, and ss showed 5173 already held by another agent's esbuild harness, so my run would have silently exercised somebody else's build. The orchestrator's clean-tree figure of 84 passed at fc0b9e5 stands, and the render-condition change cannot have moved it — at this SHA renderedGroups.has(id) is true exactly when groupStyles[id] exists, because every value is the non-empty string 'order: N' with N >= 1, so the six {#if} conditions are pointwise equivalent to the ones the 84 were measured against. Litmus test: all 8 cases in tests/unit/boardLayoutUtils.test.ts still assert real computed output of the real function with no mocks anywhere, 8 of 8 pass. What remains unverified until Task 10, now including the third derived value: (1) that orderedGroups is really derived from board.groupOrder; (2) that the computed order values match the configured sequence and the notes block stays below every group; (3) that drag & drop survives a reorder in the same session; (4) NEW — that groupClasses, groupStyles and renderedGroups stay in agreement. Before fc0b9e5 groupStyles was the single source for both the order value and the {#if} condition, so divergence was structurally impossible; now three parallel derivations off orderedGroups are held in sync only by convention, and nothing asserts that a rendered wrapper always carries both a width class and a non-zero order. The code reviewer's argument for the split is sound (a future numeric order would make position 0 falsy and silently drop the first group), so this is not a regression — but it is a slightly larger unverified surface, and finding 1 says what Task 10 should assert to close it. Two minor findings, neither blocking; both are handoffs rather than work for Task 07.

findings.location: src/ui/BoardLayout.svelte:34-53 (orderedGroups existence guard, plus the groupClasses / groupStyles / renderedGroups trio)
findings.issue: Carried forward from round-1 finding 2, re-assessed in the guard's new form. The branch 'id is in board.groupOrder but board.groups has no such key → skip it' is still reached by no test at fc0b9e5, and the round-2 rewrite left its reachability unchanged (verified: every value class that would distinguish Object.hasOwn from the old truthiness check already throws inside migrateData before render). The uncovered surface grew slightly: the {#if} conditions moved off groupStyles onto a third derived value, renderedGroups, so the previous structural guarantee — one record served as both the order source and the render condition, and could not disagree with itself — is now a convention that three separate reactive statements have to keep. Nothing asserts the invariant. Silent failure modes if it ever breaks: a wrapper rendered without an entry in groupClasses loses its width class, and one rendered without an entry in groupStyles falls back to order 0 and jumps ahead of every other group — neither raises an error, and the unit suite cannot see either, since it pins only the pure function's contract.
findings.recommendation: Confirming the round-1 routing: Task 10 is the right owner and the scenario is executable there — window.__test.resetData(snapshot with version) hands the snapshot to migrateData, and a board whose groups object lacks one key survives migration with groupOrder still naming it (probed at fc0b9e5), so the seeded board reaches BoardLayout exactly as intended. Two cautions. First, Task 10's file is already fully written: it enumerates fourteen scenarios and its Acceptance Criteria says 'со всеми четырнадцатью сценариями', so a decisions-log entry alone is droppable. Word the entry imperatively as a required fifteenth scenario, or add the checkbox to the task file. Second, ask Task 10 for one extra universal assertion alongside the seeded case, which closes the three-derivation gap for every scenario at once: for every [data-group-container] present in the DOM, assert it carries exactly one of --full / --half / --half-alone AND a computed order that parses to a number >= 1, and assert the wrapper count equals the number of visible groups. The seeded case itself stays as agreed — delete groups.orgIntentions while groupOrder still lists it, then assert the board renders, five wrappers resolve, and their order values are dense 1..5 with no gap. Cheaper alternative worth weighing before Task 08 adds a second writer to groupOrder: move the three-line derivation (filter by hidden + existence, map to fullWidth) out of the component into src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts, where it becomes directly unit-testable today and — see finding 2 — where npx tsc --noEmit actually gates it. That would give the branch a real owner instead of a single e2e scenario, and Task 10 would then only need the render-level assertions.

findings.location: src/ui/BoardLayout.svelte:35 (Object.hasOwn) vs tsconfig.json lib/target and esbuild.config.mjs:14
findings.issue: Concrete evidence that the unverifiable-file gap from finding 1 is not theoretical: the round-2 guard introduced the only ES2022 API in the whole codebase, and no gate can see it. grep over src/ and tests/ finds Object.hasOwn at exactly one site and no other ES2022+ builtin anywhere. Both declared language floors are lower: tsconfig.json sets target ES2021 with lib ['ES2021','DOM','DOM.Iterable'], and esbuild.config.mjs:14 sets target 'es2021'. Measured at fc0b9e5 in an isolated worktree: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 on the tree as it stands, but the identical call placed in a .ts file under src/ fails with TS2550 'Property hasOwn does not exist on type ObjectConstructor. Try changing the lib compiler option to es2022 or later'. tsc never parses .svelte, esbuild strips types without checking APIs and does not polyfill builtins, and no test executes the filter — so all three gates are blind to it at once. On runtime consequence I am deliberately not alarmist: Object.hasOwn needs Chrome 93+ / Safari 15.4+, Obsidian desktop is far past that on every version at minAppVersion 1.0.0, and the current Obsidian mobile app requires iOS 16, so despite manifest.json declaring isDesktopOnly false the practical exposure is limited to users pinned to an old mobile build on iOS below 15.4. The finding is about the gate blind spot and the contract mismatch, not an imminent breakage.
findings.recommendation: Not work for Task 07 to redo under pressure — the guard is correct and the security auditor's reasoning for it is sound. Pick one of two closes. (a) Preferred, and it also discharges finding 1: move the derivation into src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts. The call then sits in a .ts file that npx tsc --noEmit does gate, so the mismatch surfaces immediately instead of hiding, and the branch becomes unit-testable in the same move. (b) If the derivation stays in the component, replace Object.hasOwn(board.groups, id) with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(board.groups, id) — one line, no dependency added, identical prototype-chain soundness (that is precisely what the security auditor asked for), and it keeps the file inside the es2021 floor that the rest of the codebase and both build configs declare. Either way, record in the decisions log that .svelte files are checked by no type gate, since this is the second Task-07 issue to come out of that gap.
